paper.abstract: We present an experimental proposal to test whether gravity can entangle a levitated particle with an array of quantum clocks. paper.title: Instabilities of Simpson-Visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics
paper.abstract: We study the linear stability of Simpson-Visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). The metric contains two parameters: the mass $M$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2M$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2M$ to wormholes. The stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a Schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. All space-times under study are found to be unstable, and the corresponding exponential growth rates are calculated. For black holes the results are obtained without complications, while the wormhole stability problem faces difficulties that seem to be previously unnoticed. Thus, the Darboux transformation, used to remove the wall shaped $\approx 2/z^2$ in the effective potentials at wormhole throats ($z$ is the tortoise coordinate), creates nonphysical poles outside the throat for $a/(2M) \lesssim 4.98$. We circumvent this difficulty by using a gauge-invariant approach in the spirit of Cremona, Pizzocchero and Sarbach, leading to a master equation with a simple and regular potential. Its further analysis reveals unstable modes: the mode with a variable throat radius is always present; for $a/(2M) \gtrsim 4.98$ there are two real growing throat modes, which merge into a complex-conjugate pair (oscillatory instability) for smaller $a$. A further analysis reveals three exceptional points that separate ranges of $a/(2M)$ with different perturbation regimes. Furthermore, the leading unstable black-hole and wormhole modes approach the same limiting growth rate $Mκ\simeq 0.10121$ as $a/(2M)$ approaches unity from either side.

paper.title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate
paper.abstract: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. Periodic flux modulations may arise from the orbital motion of black holes in close binaries, while relativistic jet precession can provide an additional source of periodic variability. Such periodic signatures therefore motivate us to identify close binary candidates. Here, we report an optical periodicity of $269^{+13}_{-14}$ days in both Zwicky Transient Facility g and r bands of the blazar PKS 0301-243, with corrected global significances of $2.75σ$ and $2.18σ$, respectively. This signal persists over 7 cycles across a baseline of ~2000 days. We interpret this period as a possible modulation associated with the orbital motion of a supermassive black hole binary. A longer optical periodicity of $889^{+47}_{-46}$ days is identified in Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope, with corrected global significance of $1.97σ$. The longer periodicity spans approximately 5 cycles over a baseline of ~4500 days, potentially associated with jet precession. Both periodicities are independently identified using multiple methods. A supermassive black hole binary incorporating a relativistic jet and a circumbinary disc could reproduce the observed light curve ensemble. For a total mass of $10^{8.95} M_\odot$ and a mass ratio q = 0.1, the derived milli-parsec separation and a short gravitational wave driven coalescence time, $t_c = 1122^{+144}_{-144}$ years, imply that PKS 0301-243 may be a rare source of nano-hertz gravitational waves and a potential multimessenger laboratory for the terminal stages of supermassive black hole coalescence.

paper.abstract: We present an analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5, an extremely cold Y dwarf identified in the JADES/GOODS-South field. Using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging spanning a $\simeq2$-yr baseline, we calibrate the JWST astrometry and obtain the first robust parallax measurement for a brown dwarf discovered in a JWST extragalactic deep field. We measure a proper motion of $μ_{\rm tot}=49.8^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and a parallax of $\varpi=15.7^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ mas, corresponding to a geometric distance of $d=64^{+6}_{-5}$ pc, $\sim3\times$ further than that of the previously known most distant Y dwarfs with parallax-measured distances. We hence determine a tangential velocity of $v_{\rm tan}=15.0^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ km s$^{-1}$, consistent with a Galactic thin-disk object. We find no evidence for binary acceleration, significant photometric variability, or a plausible host. The $J$-band spectral morphology of JADES-GS-BD-5 is consistent with existing Y-dwarf templates, while its extremely faint luminosity and overall near-infrared spectral profile confirm that it is one of the coldest dwarfs discovered to date. We therefore adopt a classification of $>$Y1, consistent with a NIRCam colour-based proxy of cY1.5. The robust parallax-determined distance allows us to determine its bolometric luminosity, $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\odot})=-7.08^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$. Evolutionary modelling places JADES-GS-BD-5 in the planetary-mass regime and makes it a rare benchmark for the study of cold giant-planet atmospheres. Current atmospheric models fail to reproduce its SED in detail, pointing to the importance of disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing. Finally, we also report additional proper motion measurements for eight of the other nine known JADES Y-dwarf candidates, highlighting JWST extragalactic surveys as a powerful route to building a statistically useful, parallax-calibrated sample of Y dwarfs.

paper.title: When Can Pulsar Timing Distinguish a Propagation Mass from a Weak Longitudinal Background?
paper.abstract: A weak longitudinal background can imitate the angular response of a gravitational-wave propagation mass. We quantify this ambiguity in a compressed Gaussian experiment constructed from the NANOGrav 15-year timing data. At a false-alarm probability of $10^{-3}$, allowing a weak longitudinal component in a massless background costs at least 16.29 percentage points of optimal rejection power for a specified source in a 20-pulsar subarray. Expanding the array to 40 pulsars at the same background level recovers at least 7.62 points. In a separate low-background experiment, we allow the same continuous range of longitudinal amplitudes at zero and positive mass. Across that range and three injected background levels, one test rejects zero mass with at least 97.38\% power at either of two masses separated by 1.08\%. With false assignment limited to $10^{-3}$ at the other mass, the power to identify either mass is at most 1.584\%. A cutoff can thus be identifiable before its position within a frequency cell can be resolved.

paper.title: Torsion talks only to spin: the CMB temperature as a test of energy exchange in Einstein-Cartan cosmology
paper.abstract: The cosmic microwave background temperature at $z=0.886$ is known to $2\%$ from molecular absorption towards PKS~1830$-$211; CO absorbers and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich clusters extend the measurement to $z\simeq3$. We use them on a question that cosmologies with torsion leave open. When the geometry exchanges energy with several matter components, which of them receives it? In Einstein-Cartan theory the Noether identities of each sector fix the answer. A sector's energy-momentum fails to be conserved only in proportion to its own spin, so minimally coupled light, which has none, is conserved whatever the torsion does. A metric-affine cosmology fitted to DESI DR2 distributes the exchange ``universally'' among all fluids, radiation included; the photons then gain almost a third of their energy. If the photons stay a blackbody, as FIRAS requires of any source set by local conditions, the model predicts a background colder than $T_{0}(1+z)$ by $7\%$ at $z\simeq0.9$ and by $8.5\%$ at $z\gtrsim3$, with no free parameter. PKS~1830$-$211 gives $5.08\pm0.10\,\mathrm{K}$ against a predicted $4.78\,\mathrm{K}$; with the CO absorbers it favours the standard scaling by $Δχ^{2}=13$, and 18 Planck cluster bins give $χ^{2}=50.8$ versus $15.5$. Under the same reading the primary anisotropies would change their spectral shape by amounts Planck excludes. If dark matter carries the spin instead, $H(z)$ moves by less than $10^{-4}$ below $z=3$ at the fitted parameters and $T(z)$ is standard again.

paper.title: The three-dimensional Galilean black hole
paper.abstract: We report a novel solution of three-dimensional Galilean Anti-de Sitter gravity. The theory can be formulated as a topological gauge theory invariant under the doubly extended Newton-Hooke group in three dimensions. The solution possesses four conserved charges: energy, angular momentum, spin and rest mass. Interestingly, the magnitude of the spin turns out to bounded from above by the rest mass. The solution exhibits the thermal properties that define a black hole configuration in terms of its gauge theoretical description. Temperature, angular velocity and other chemical potentials are obtained from suitable regularity conditions associated with the topology of the Euclidean continuation of the solution. At zero temperature, an extreme configuration is shown to emerge provided the bound between the spin and the rest mass saturates.

paper.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
paper.abstract: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs. For individual DMs, the correlation with the bandpowers is at the per cent level. Neglecting the cross-covariance changes the width of the $χ^2$ distribution by only 0.8 per cent, so the two observables can be treated as effectively independent for wide-area surveys. In a joint forecast with an LSST-like weak lensing survey, adding the Macquart relation tightens constraints on the physical baryon density by 32 per cent and on the mean host contribution by a factor of 4.1, while improving baryonification parameters by only about 5 per cent, indirectly through the host contribution. Finally, we show that the redshift distribution of FRBs without identified hosts, which enters every DM power spectrum, can be reconstructed by inverting their DMs with the jointly fitted mean relation without biasing the inferred parameters, whereas a 20 per cent error in the mean relation biases the DM power spectrum by up to 2$σ$ per band for $5\times 10^5$ FRBs.
